description: Independent ground-truth labels for login_brute_force_events.jsonl, kept separate from the log data itself — matching how Stage 5 replay evaluation compares compiled-rule output against independently labelled events, not against labels baked into the log.

scenarios.description: Exactly the canonical example from SF-SAMPLE-001: 5 failures in 95s, then a success.
scenarios.note: Primary positive case — this is the scenario the report and the hand-written IR both describe.

scenarios.description: Only 2 failures before success — below the 5-failure threshold.
scenarios.note: Tests that the threshold is enforced, not just 'any failure before success'.

scenarios.description: 6 failures, no subsequent success at all.
scenarios.note: Tests that a rule requiring the 'success' step does not fire on failures alone — this is a real brute-force attempt that simply didn't (yet) succeed, and is intentionally out of scope for this specific behaviour.

scenarios.description: A single successful login with no preceding failures.
5 failures, but spread across 10 minutes, then a success — only the last failure falls inside the 2-minute window before the success.
scenarios.note: Edge case that specifically tests time-window precision, not just threshold counting. A rule that counts failures without windowing would incorrectly alert here.

scenarios.description: 5 failures in 60s, then a success — same shape as scenario A, different account.
scenarios.note: Second positive case, to confirm the rule generalises across accounts rather than being keyed to svc-backup01 specifically.
